question: How do I evaluate buying vs building sales-data infrastructure?
answer:
**Buy if you're <$20M ARR or lack internal data engineers. Build if you're >$50M ARR, have a data team, and have specific workflow gaps.** Most companies should buy. Time-to-value is 4 weeks (vs. 6 months building), you shift risk to vendor, and you avoid hiring overhead. **"Buy" vendors to evaluate:** 1. **Clari** ($80–150K/year): Best for forecast + deal health. If your #1 problem is forecast accuracy, buy here. ROI: 6–9 months. 2. **Salesforce Einstein** (bundled): Comes with Salesforce. Opportunity scoring, forecasting, anomaly detection. ROI: immediate (no new cost). Limitation: can't customize much. 3. **Tableau or Looker** ($30–80K/year): Self-service dashboards. Buy if your team is drowning in ad-hoc report requests. ROI: 3–4 months (saves RevOps time). 4. **Apollo, Hunter, ZoomInfo** ($10–60K/year each): Lead enrichment. Buy if you're doing outbound and prospect data is stale. ROI: 2–3 months (improves outbound conversion by 5–10%). 5. **Slack integration layers** (Slack-Salesforce, Slack-Clari): $5–20K/year. Buy if reps don't log into Salesforce (they check Slack instead). ROI: immediate (hidden cost avoidance). **When "Build" makes sense:** 1. **You have a data engineering team** (≥2 FTE). They can assemble Salesforce + HubSpot + Stripe + Zendesk data into a data warehouse, then build custom dashboards. 2. **You have a unique workflow** (none of the vendors do it). Example: You need "days-from-qualified-to-close" scored for each rep in real-time (most vendors can't do this). 3. **You're at $50M+ ARR** (cost of in-house team is <$200K/year; ROI is obvious). 4. **You've already tried 2–3 vendors and they all failed** (usually because of data quality, not the vendor's fault). Building won't fix that. **Real cost comparison ($20M ARR company, 50 reps):** | Scenario | Buy (Clari + Tableau) | Build (1 Engineer + 1 Analyst) | |----------|----------------------|---------------------------| | Year 1 Cost | $120K | $180K (salary + benefits) | | Year 1 Implementation | 4 weeks | 4 months | | Time to Forecast Improvement | Month 1 | Month 6 | | Customization | 30 min to change dashboard | 1 week to change logic | | Maintenance | Vendor handles | Your team maintains | | **Verdict** | Buy (lower risk) | Build if forecast still bad | **Decision tree:** Start here: 1. **What's your #1 pain point?** - "Forecast is wrong every month." → Buy Clari. - "Can't get dashboards fast enough." → Buy Tableau. - "Prospect data is stale." → Buy Apollo/ZoomInfo. - "Don't know which deals are really at risk." → Buy Clari or Salesforce Einstein. 2. **Can a vendor solve it?** - Yes → Buy (see above vendors). Commit 12 months. - No → Investigate "why." Usually it's data quality (CRM is a mess), not the vendor. 3. **If "no," do you have a data team?** - Yes → Build a bespoke integration. - No → Fix your CRM first. The vendor isn't the problem. **Typical build failure pattern:** "We'll hire a data engineer and build a custom forecast model." → Month 1: Engineer gets Salesforce access, learns it's a mess. → Month 2–3: Engineer fixes CRM (that's the real work). → Month 4: Engineer builds first dashboard (forecast dashboard). → Month 5–6: Dashboard needs tuning (why does forecast still not match?). CRM data is still bad. → Month 9: You've spent $25K and your forecast is still wrong. Meanwhile, Clari would've solved it in 4 weeks for $10K. **The rule:** If your CRM is a disaster, **no vendor or in-house team can help** until you fix it. Fix CRM first (see Q113). Then evaluate buy vs build. **Action:** If <$50M ARR, buy Clari + Tableau (8-week trial). If forecast improves + adoption is >80%, commit. If not, your problem is CRM data quality (not the vendor).
